questions.question: Which statement best defines the purpose of Circuit Breaker Simulator?
options: A circuit breaker stops calls to an unhealthy dependency after a failure threshold, then probes recovery instead of allowing a cascade.
It is only a visual dashboard with no decision model.
It is a storage engine that replaces every system dependency.
It guarantees a production design without workload evidence.
questions.explanation: A circuit breaker stops calls to an unhealthy dependency after a failure threshold, then probes recovery instead of allowing a cascade. The tool structures this decision; it does not remove the need to validate assumptions.

questions.question: What information should be established before relying on Circuit Breaker Simulator?
options: Only the name of a preferred vendor.
Set failure rate, request volume, timeout, opening threshold, cooldown, and half-open probe behavior.
questions.explanation: Set failure rate, request volume, timeout, opening threshold, cooldown, and half-open probe behavior. Explicit inputs keep the result tied to a reviewable workload rather than a generic recommendation.

questions.question: How should the output of Circuit Breaker Simulator be interpreted?
options: Treat it as proof that no failure can occur.
Ignore the assumptions once a result appears.
Observe rejected calls, dependency load, recovery time, and user-visible fallback rather than treating an open circuit as success.
Choose the largest result without reviewing trade-offs.
questions.explanation: Observe rejected calls, dependency load, recovery time, and user-visible fallback rather than treating an open circuit as success. The result is evidence for a design review, not an automatic production guarantee.

questions.question: Which experiment best tests whether the current Circuit Breaker Simulator result is robust?
options: Keep every input at its default value.
Skip the failure and boundary cases.
Introduce intermittent recovery and tune half-open probes so the service recovers without immediately causing another overload.
questions.explanation: Introduce intermittent recovery and tune half-open probes so the service recovers without immediately causing another overload. Changing a consequential assumption exposes where the current design stops being safe.
